response.original_text: SWIRLING PINK AND PURPLE IN SPACE NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope showcased a breathtaking image of spiral galaxy NGC 4258, featuring its arms created by a central supermassive black hole. “In this composite view, NASA Chandra X-ray’s data (royal blue) show superheated shockwaves created by central black hole jets, along with Hubble's optical data (red, yellow, pale blue) and NASA Webb’s infrared view of dust filaments (orange),” the space agency wrote on Tuesday. The galaxy is located approximately 24 million light-years from Earth in the constellation Canes Venatici. (Instagram/NASA Hubble)
